title: Tierwise evaluate vector
description: One evaluate vector (spec section 12.3): one resolve or decide call against a bundle file, with the expected result or the expected error. This schema checks structure only. Cross-references (bundle paths, level names, clause existence, id equal to path, unique ids) and runner behaviour are checked elsewhere ([VEC-19], [VEC-112]).

id.description: Vector identifier. It equals the file path relative to evaluate/, without the .yaml extension ([VEC-11], [VEC-12]).

specVersion.description: Version of this specification that the vector targets. The value for this version is "0.1" ([VEC-14]).

clauses.description: Clause IDs that define the behaviour the vector checks. Each entry is a clause ID from spec.md or a section ([VEC-16]).

description.description: One non-empty, single-line sentence that says what the vector checks ([VEC-17]).

call.description: The one operation that the runner invokes: resolve or decide ([VEC-21]).

sync.description: When true, the runner invokes the synchronous variant of the operation instead of the provider-capable one ([VEC-25]).

bundle.description: Path to the bundle file, relative to the directory that contains this vector file ([VEC-22]). The resolved file must lie in bundles/ or in bundles/invalid/ ([VEC-23]). The pattern checks only the form: no leading / or \, no drive letter, no backslash, and a final bundles/<file> or bundles/invalid/<file> segment. The runner checks that the path resolves to the suite's own bundles/ directory, and a path that resolves elsewhere is a runner failure ([VEC-23]).

context.description: Caller-supplied context for the operation. When present it must be a mapping. Its members levels and axes may be omitted, and their values are passed as written, so that malformed values can be tested ([VEC-28], [VEC-33], [CTX-1]). A member other than levels and axes is also passed as written, so that the operation raises E_CONTEXT_INVALID for it ([CTX-2]).

key.description: The key to resolve. Required on a resolve vector and forbidden on a decide vector ([VEC-29]). An empty string is a valid value that tests the lookup ([EVAL-37]).

feature.description: The feature to decide. Required on a decide vector and forbidden on a resolve vector ([VEC-29]). An empty string is a valid value that tests the lookup ([EVAL-37]).

input.description: The FactSet passed to decide, as the YAML 1.2 core schema produces it, with no conversion ([VEC-31]). Any YAML value is allowed here, including null and shapes that are malformed, because the shape is checked by the operation under test ([FACT-22], [EVAL-36]). Its shape follows the FactSet form of section 3: a map with optional members facts and children. Required on decide and forbidden on resolve ([VEC-30], [VEC-32]).

providers.description: Stubs for the service-sourced levels of the bundle. Each level name maps to the marker none, or to a stub that maps node IDs to outcomes ([VEC-37]). A level that is omitted gets an empty stub ([VEC-39]).

exact.description: When true, each mapping in the actual result must have exactly the keys that expect names at that position, and provider calls outside providerCalls count as mismatches ([VEC-62] to [VEC-67]). Defaults to false, which compares only the named fields ([VEC-54]).

expect.description: The expected outcome. It is either an error form with one error code, or a result form that names at least one result field. Either form may also carry providerCalls ([VEC-48], [VEC-49]). Its shape depends on call, as the conditions of this schema state.

allOf.description: A resolve vector has key, has no feature and no input ([VEC-29], [VEC-32]). Its expect is a resolve expectation.
A decide vector has feature and input, and has no key ([VEC-29], [VEC-30]). Its expect is a decide expectation.
A decide call and a synchronous call call no provider, so every provider call count that these vectors name is 0 ([SVC-22], [EVAL-42], [VEC-26]).

When exact is true and the expectation is a result form, the expectation names every member of the Resolved result, closed under the result shape of section 9 ([VEC-63], [PROV-11]). It may also name providerCalls.

When exact is true and the expectation is a result form, the expectation names every member of the Decision result, closed under the result shape of section 9 ([VEC-63], [PROV-63]). It may also name providerCalls.

clauseId.description: A clause ID: an area prefix from spec.md, a hyphen and a number from 1 ([VEC-16]).

zeroProviderCalls.description: Provider invocation counts for a vector in which no provider can be called, namely a decide vector and a vector with sync true ([SVC-22], [EVAL-42]). Each count is 0 or the expectation can never be met ([VEC-65]).

additionalProperties.description: Map from node ID to the expected number of provider invocations, which is 0.

errorCode.description: An evaluation error code that the evaluation operations may raise: the eleven codes of [EVAL-38] (requirements 6.2). Error messages are not compared ([VEC-52]). E_PROVENANCE_INVALID is a tooling code for provenance cases and is not one of them.

context.description: The caller-supplied context: a mapping with optional members levels and axes ([VEC-28], [CTX-2]). A null context is a runner failure ([VEC-68]). The def does not close the mapping: a context that has any other member must reach the operation unchanged, because [CTX-2] makes that an E_CONTEXT_INVALID error, which a vector can expect. This follows the treatment of input, whose shape is also checked by the operation ([VEC-31]). A misspelt member name in a vector therefore shows as an error that the vector did not expect, not as a schema failure.

levels.description: Map from non-root level names to node IDs. Keys are strings. Values are passed as written, so a malformed map or value, such as a list, null or an integer, can be tested ([CTX-1], [VEC-33]). Omitted means an empty map ([CTX-2]).

axes.description: Map from axis names to node IDs, with the same rules as levels ([CTX-1], [CTX-2]).

providers.description: Map from a service-sourced level name to the marker none, or to a stub ([VEC-37]). Level names must name a service-sourced level of the bundle, except where the vector expects E_EVALUATOR_OPTIONS ([VEC-38]).

additionalProperties.description: Either the marker none, which registers no provider and so makes creating the evaluator fail with E_PROVIDER_MISSING ([VEC-40]), or a stub ([VEC-37]).

stub.description: Map from node ID to the outcome that the provider returns for that node. A node that the stub does not list must not be called ([VEC-46]).

nodeOutcome.description: The outcome for one node. It has exactly one of two forms: values, which the provider returns, or fail, which makes the provider fail ([VEC-41]).

oneOf.description: Values form: a provider result that returns the listed key names and values for the node ([VEC-42]). An empty map returns no entries ([SVC-36]). A null in place of the map is a runner failure ([VEC-41]).

values.description: Map from key names to the YAML values that the provider returns, passed through without conversion ([VEC-42], [VEC-33]).

oneOf.description: Fail form: the provider fails for this node with the given outcome ([VEC-43]).

fail.description: The fail outcome: unavailable or timeout. Both give identical results ([VEC-44], [SVC-23], [SVC-39]).

providerCalls.description: Expected provider invocation counts: a map from level name to a map from node ID to a non-negative count ([VEC-65]). A count of 0 asserts that the node was not called ([SVC-19]).

additionalProperties.description: Map from node ID to the expected number of provider invocations for that level and node.
Number of provider invocations, counting fail outcomes ([VEC-47]).

errorForm.description: The error form of expect: one error code and no result field ([VEC-48], [VEC-50]). It may also carry providerCalls ([VEC-65]).

error.description: The expected error code. It is the only normative part of an error ([VEC-52]).

providerCalls.description: Expected provider invocation counts, which may accompany the error ([VEC-65]).

resolveExpect.description: Expectation for a resolve vector. Either the error form, or the result form, which names at least one Resolved field and no error ([VEC-48], [VEC-49]). Fields are compared as a subset unless exact is true ([VEC-54]).

then.description: A commutative key has no source, so naming one can never match ([PROV-45], [VEC-55]).

strategy.description: Expected merge strategy, the value of combine ([PROV-13]).

kind.description: Expected kind name. Present only when the key opts into a kind ([PROV-14], [PROV-15]).

value.description: Expected value in the JSON encoding of its type. An expected null matches only an actual null ([VEC-56]). Values are not canonicalised by the runner ([VEC-60]).

bundleVersion.description: Expected bundleVersion of the loaded bundle ([PROV-18]).

skippedScopes.description: Expected skipped scopes, in order ([PROV-58]). An expected empty list matches only an empty actual list ([VEC-61]).

contributions.description: Expected contribution entries, in evaluation-path order ([PROV-34]). An expected empty list matches only an empty actual list ([VEC-61]).

source.description: Expected source of an order-dependent value: the string DEFAULT, or a source object ([PROV-46]). Present only for override and deep_merge keys ([PROV-45]).

providerCalls.description: Expected provider invocation counts for the resolve call ([VEC-65]).

decideExpect.description: Expectation for a decide vector. Either the error form, or the result form, which names at least one Decision field and no error ([VEC-48], [VEC-49]). decide calls no provider, so providerCalls counts are 0 when named ([VEC-26], [SVC-22]).

then.description: A MISSING_FACT decision has an empty trace, so a non-empty expected trace can never match ([PROV-84], [VEC-61]).

effect.description: Expected effect that the decision returns, in the form of the feature's returns declaration: a string, null or an object ([PROV-65] to [PROV-67]). It is compared unchanged.

bundleVersion.description: Expected bundleVersion of the loaded bundle ([PROV-18]).

policy.description: Expected name of the policy of the selected binding ([PROV-71]).

reason.description: Expected reason, one of the RULE, DEFAULT or MISSING_FACT objects ([PROV-73]).

trace.description: Expected trace entries, in rule order ([PROV-82]). An expected empty list matches only an empty actual list ([VEC-61]).

providerCalls.description: Expected provider invocation counts. A decide call makes none, so each count is 0 when named; the conditions of the schema enforce this ([SVC-22], [VEC-65]).

expectSource.description: Expected source object of an order-dependent value: the winning scope, and its node when the scope is not the root level ([PROV-46], [PROV-47]). Structure only.

scope.description: Scope kind of the winning scope.

name.description: Declared name of the winning scope.

node.description: Node ID of the winning scope. Present only when the scope is not the root level.

expectSkippedScope.description: Expected skipped scope entry ([PROV-54]). Its reason is UNKNOWN_NODE, the only reason in this version ([PROV-55]).

scope.description: Scope kind of the skipped scope.

name.description: Declared name of the skipped scope.

node.description: Unknown node ID that the context supplied.

reason.description: Reason for the skip. The only value in this version ([PROV-55]).

expectContribution.description: Expected contribution entry ([PROV-22] to [PROV-36]). A member that the result omits under its provenance clause must be absent here when exact is true ([VEC-64]). In every case a member that the entry cannot carry is forbidden, because a named key that the actual lacks never matches ([VEC-55]): onSourceFailure on a value entry ([PROV-32]), and value on a failure entry under skip ([PROV-30]).

allOf.description: A value entry has no onSourceFailure. A value entry is one whose effect is a value label ([PROV-32]).
A failure entry under skip has no value ([PROV-30]).
An entry that carries onSourceFailure is a failure entry, so its effect is UNAVAILABLE or INVALID when named ([PROV-32], [PROV-41]).

scope.description: Scope kind of the contributing scope.

name.description: Declared name of the contributing scope.

node.description: Node ID of the contributing scope. Present only when the scope is not the root level ([PROV-25]).

value.description: Value that the scope contributes, or the deny value of a failure entry under deny. Absent for a failure entry under skip ([PROV-27], [PROV-30]). Never null ([PROV-31]), so an expected null can never match.

effect.description: Contribution label: a value label, or the failure label UNAVAILABLE or INVALID ([PROV-24], [PROV-38], [PROV-41]).

onSourceFailure.description: Source-failure behaviour in effect for the key. Present only on a failure entry ([PROV-32], [PROV-33]).

expectBinding.description: Expected selected binding: its level, and its node when the level is not the root level ([PROV-68], [PROV-69]).

node.description: Node ID of the selected binding. Present only when the level is not the root level.

expectReason.description: Expected reason of a decision: an object whose type is RULE, DEFAULT or MISSING_FACT ([PROV-73]). A member that the named type cannot carry is forbidden, because a named key that the actual lacks never matches ([VEC-55], [PROV-74] to [PROV-76]). Members may be omitted, because matching is by subset unless exact is true ([VEC-54]).

allOf.description: A RULE reason has no facts ([PROV-74]).
A DEFAULT reason has no id, name or facts ([PROV-75]).
A MISSING_FACT reason has no id or name ([PROV-76]).
No reason has both facts and a rule member, whatever its type is, because id and name belong to RULE and facts to MISSING_FACT ([PROV-74], [PROV-76]).

id.description: Id of the winning rule. Present only when type is RULE ([PROV-74]).

name.description: Name of the winning rule. Present only when type is RULE ([PROV-74]).

facts.description: Missing fact names, in the order of [RULE-44]. Present only when type is MISSING_FACT ([PROV-76], [PROV-77]). The list is never empty ([RULE-42]).

expectTraceEntry.description: Expected trace entry for one rule checked ([PROV-78] to [PROV-81]). failed is forbidden when matched is true, because it is present only when matched is false ([PROV-80]).

id.description: Id of the rule that the entry describes.

failed.description: First failing condition. Present if and only if matched is false ([PROV-80]).

fact.description: Name of the fact of the failing condition.
